column7: TRIGGER-INTEGRITY-1 item 1 (docs/design/trigger-rowdigest.md, Definition versions). The periodic trigger integrity check treated any definition that was not exactly this binary's as tampering and re-installed its own, so during a rolling upgrade to a release that changes a trigger function (as the search_path pin of #3631 did) old and new replicas reverted each other every tick: SECURITY lines and tamper increments on both sides, fleet-wide cache flushes, DROP/CREATE TRIGGER under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, and old replicas undoing the newer security fix part of the time. Each function now carries a version marker comment (version plus SHA-256 of body, settings and trigger shape); a checker or installer leaves a self-consistent definition at most one version ahead in place (non-SECURITY warning, reason=newer_definition, one flush) and still restores anything else, including a forged marker whose digest does not match. Also TestSecretNodeCacheEpochIntegrity_NewerReleaseDefinitionIsLeftInPlace_Postgres (red on main by behaviour), TestTriggerIntegrityVersions_TwoReleasesTickAlternately_Postgres, _ForgedMarkersAreTampering_Postgres, _CacheEpochTwoReleasesTickAlternately_Postgres, TestTriggerDefMarker_NewerThan. The digest is not a signature: the function owner can forge a self-consistent marker one version ahead; a checker leaves it in place for at most triggerDefNewerAcceptBound (24 h) from its first reading of it, then logs SECURITY, counts tamper and restores its own (ask 3841-forged-marker-acceptance-bound, option a; TestTriggerIntegrityNewerBound_ForgedMarkerRestoredAfterBound_Postgres, _CacheEpochForgedMarkerRestoredAfterBound_Postgres, _RebootDoesNotProtectExpiredMarker_Postgres). Residual: within the bound the forged definition stays (hourly warning, newer_definition counter); the clock is per process, so a replica restart starts it again.
